confirm.title: Add a D.A.R.S. receiver
confirm.description: Do you want to set up {name}?

user.title: Add a D.A.R.S. receiver
user.description: How is the receiver connected to Home Assistant?

pick_bluetooth.title: Add a D.A.R.S. receiver
pick_bluetooth.description: Select the D.A.R.S. receiver to connect to over Bluetooth.

usb.title: Receiver on USB
usb.description: Plug the receiver into this Home Assistant machine and switch it to USB mode in the D.A.R.S. app. Then choose its serial port (D.A.R.S. boards show as Espressif).

network.title: Receiver on the network
network.description: For the M5Stack ToughC5's RS485 port through an RS485-to-Ethernet bridge (for example Waveshare RS485 TO ETH (B)) set to TCP server, 115200 baud, 8N1. Enter the bridge's IP address and TCP port.

error.cannot_open: Could not open that serial port. Check the port and that no other program is using it.
error.no_data_usb: The port opened but no D.A.R.S. data arrived. Make sure the receiver is in USB mode.
error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to that address and port.
error.no_data_network: Connected, but no D.A.R.S. data arrived. Check the bridge's serial settings (115200 baud, 8N1) and the RS485 A/B wiring.

abort.no_devices_found: No unconfigured D.A.R.S. receivers were found in Bluetooth range. Make sure the device is powered on and nearby.

init.title: D.A.R.S. options
init.description: The FAA lookup sends the serial number of each drone the receiver picks up to the public FAA UAS Declaration of Compliance database (uasdoc.faa.gov) to show its declared make and model. Turn it off to keep everything on your local network.

data.faa_lookup: Look up drone make and model online
